subject.title: improve(telegram): align QA coverage with startup behavior

question: Should `telegram.startup-getme` retain its product-startup coverage claim when deterministic owner-path tests pass but the dedicated live Gateway scenario is blocked for lack of a leased Telegram credential?
rationale: This is a release-evidence standard rather than a mechanical code correction: maintainers must choose whether the claim requires a successful credentialed run or may rely on deterministic product-owner outcomes plus an explicit blocked live check.

options.title: Require positive live proof
options.body: Keep the target scoped as incomplete until a redacted leased-credential run proves the real Gateway `startAccount` path.

options.title: Accept bounded deterministic coverage
options.body: Accept the current branch if release reporting clearly preserves that live credential proof is blocked rather than passed.

options.title: Split the target
options.body: Land the deterministic outcome coverage but move the live product-startup claim into a separate taxonomy target until credentials are available.

recommendation.title: Require positive live proof
recommendation.body: Keep the target scoped as incomplete until a redacted leased-credential run proves the real Gateway `startAccount` path.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied history ties this contributor to the problem statement, scenario design, and current implementation; a broader current-main ownership trail was not available in the hydrated context.
